idiom_name: hand-written struct over map[K]V implementing the interface (implicit satisfaction)
implementation_notes: Go interfaces are satisfied structurally, so the fake is an ordinary struct with methods over a map: no framework, no implements declaration and no generated code, which is why the hand-written fake is the community's standard test double and what this row calls a cheap working implementation. The standard library even ships domain fakes ready-made - testing/fstest.MapFS is an in-memory file system for tests and net/http/httptest serves real HTTP in-process - so prefer those when the collaborator is a file system or an HTTP service. Add a compile-time assertion such as var _ UserRepository = (*fakeUsers)(nil) so interface drift fails the build, and guard the map if tests run with t.Parallel().
pitfalls: A map without a mutex is a data race as soon as a test runs with t.Parallel or the code under test spawns goroutines - and the race detector only reports it under -race.
The fake drifts from the real adapter silently; keep the interface assertion and at least one test against the real implementation.
Returning zero values where the real collaborator returns a typed error (fs.ErrNotExist and friends) changes the caller's error handling - mirror the real sentinel errors.
